results.title: Determining evapotranspiration of Faba bean and Chickpea using the soil water balance method under field conditions in in the Gezira Scheme, Sudan | Discover Agriculture | Springer Nature Link
results.description: # Determining evapotranspiration of Faba bean and Chickpea using the soil water balance method under field conditions in in the Gezira Scheme, Sudan. Water scarcity is a major constraint to agricultural productivity in Sudan, making the accurate estimation of crop water requirements (CWRs) essential for efficient irrigation management. This study quantified crop evapotranspiration (ETc) and developed growth-stage-specific crop coefficients (Kc) for faba bean (*Vicia faba* L.) and chickpea (*Cicer arietinum* L.) under field conditions in the Gezira Scheme, Sudan. ETc was determined using the soil water balance method with gravimetric soil moisture measurements across four phenological stages: initial, development, mid-season, and late season, while reference evapotranspiration (ETo) was computed using the FAO Penman–Monteith approach in CROPWAT. The average seasonal ETc was 435 mm for faba bean and 380 mm for chickpea, with maximum daily values observed during the mid-season stage. Stage-specific Kc values were 0.31, 0.85, 1.07, and 0.55 for faba bean, and 0.28, 0.71, 1.04, and 0.30 for chickpea, respectively.

results.description: Soil sensors for irrigation scheduling. Soil water tension sensors are an effective tool in irrigation management, enabling producers to monitor soil water during the growing season and improve irrigation timing. The amount of water a soil can hold is influenced by many factors, such as soil texture and soil organic matter. Among the most used tools are soil water matric potential sensors, or soil water tension sensors (figure 1). These sensors deliver data that relate tension values to crop-available water. # Relationship Between Soil Water Tension and Soil Water Status. Soil water tension (SWT) is defined as the water pressure of a soil at a particular time, usually measured in kiloPascals (kPa) or centibars (cb). The saturation range goes from SWT of 0 kPa to SWT at field capacity. To achieve these efficiencies at this timing, the amount of irrigation to be applied should be calculated to bring soil water level back to field capacity (0 percent SWD).

Crop water use, also known as evapotranspiration (ET), is the water used by a crop for growth and cooling purposes. This water is extracted from the soil root zone by the root system, which represents transpiration and is no longer available as stored water in the soil. Crop water use (ET) is influenced by prevailing weather conditions, available water in the soil, crop species and growth stage. At full cover, a crop will have the maximum ET rate (reference ET) if soil water is not limited; namely if the soil root zone is at field capacity. Full cover is a growth stage at which most of the soil is shaded by the crop canopy.

The approach to follow should be selected as a function of the purpose of the calculation, the accuracy required and the data available. Where the soil is wet for most of the time from irrigation or rain, the evaporation from the soil surface will be considerable and Kc may exceed 1. Deviation of the Kc mid from the reference value '1' is primarily due to differences in crop height and resistance between the grass reference surface and the agricultural crop and weather conditions.
